text: E. coli, Staphylococcus, and Streptococcus can all enter the udder and cause mastitis in one or more mammary glands; E. coli-caused mastitis tends to be the most acute and severe. Signs: fever, brick-red eye mucous membranes, swollen/red/painful affected glands, and piglets squealing from lack of milk. Treatment: TMP+Sulfa or Amoxicillin+Colistin (see the MMA entry for acute cases). Prevention: keep the udder and environment clean, and clip piglet teeth properly to avoid cuts/lesions on the teats.
